themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street conditions in Washington Heights/Inwood have deteriorated sharply THIS WEEK with 57 complaints filed compared to a 9.6-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 492% spike (z-score: 8.22)—suggesting a possible widespread pothole, flooding, or pavement failure event requiring immediate investigation.
evidence: 57 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 9.6 weekly average (492% spike, z-score: 8.22)
351 total DOB permit filings in last 90 days with 312 alterations, suggesting ongoing construction activity that may be damaging streets
Spike appeared THIS WEEK, indicating acute rather than chronic problem
reporting_angles: What triggered the sudden surge in street damage complaints this week? Interview residents and DOT to identify specific locations and causes.
Are active construction projects contributing to street deterioration? Cross-reference DOB permits with complaint hotspots.

themes_detail.label: Park Safety and Misuse Surge
themes_detail.summary: Multiple overlapping park-related 311 spikes THIS WEEK signal potential safety and management breakdown: Noise - Park complaints up 1500% (4 THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 avg), Bike/Roller/Skate violations up 2300% (3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 avg), and Park Rules violations up 2300% (3 last week vs. 0.1 avg)—aligning with repeated community board requests for enhanced park security staff.
evidence: 4 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (1500% spike, z-score: 8.66)
3 bike/roller/skate complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
3 park rules violations last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
Community board has repeatedly requested enhanced park safety through additional security staff and police presence—unfunded need year after year
reporting_angles: Which parks in Washington Heights/Inwood are experiencing the surge in noise and rule violations? Are there specific times or user groups driving complaints?
Interview Parks Department about enforcement capacity and whether the district's long-standing budget request for enhanced park security has been addressed.

themes_detail.label: Damaged Tree Outbreak
themes_detail.summary: Tree damage complaints spiked 700% LAST WEEK with 5 complaints vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 9.04), suggesting a weather event, disease outbreak, or infrastructure failure affecting the neighborhood's urban forest.
evidence: 5 damaged tree complaints last week vs. 0.6 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 9.04)
Spike appeared last week, indicating acute event rather than long-term trend
reporting_angles: What caused the sudden tree damage last week? Investigate recent weather events, pest outbreaks, or infrastructure work that may have affected trees.
Document which neighborhoods and street blocks experienced the most tree damage to understand the geographic scope.

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Acceleration
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints jumped 188% LAST WEEK with 23 complaints compared to an 8-week average of 8.0 (z-score: 5.3), coupled with a 600% spike in unsanitary animal conditions on private property 2 weeks ago (7 vs. 1.0 avg)—indicating possible rat population surge linked to sanitation breakdowns.
evidence: 23 rodent complaints last week vs. 8.0 weekly average (188% spike, z-score: 5.3)
7 unsanitary animal private property complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.0 weekly average (600% spike, z-score: 8.49)
Community board has repeatedly requested more frequent litter basket collection from Sanitation Department—unfunded need that may be enabling rodent proliferation
reporting_angles: Is inadequate litter collection in the district creating food sources for rodents? Investigate Sanitation Department service levels in Washington Heights/Inwood.
Interview residents about where rodents are most visible and whether they've noticed changes in garbage collection frequency or quality.

themes_detail.label: Traffic Congestion Spike
themes_detail.summary: Traffic complaints surged 700% LAST WEEK with 6 complaints vs. 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 6.33), potentially linked to street condition deterioration (which spiked THIS WEEK) or concurrent construction activity affecting flow.
evidence: 6 traffic complaints last week vs. 0.8 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 6.33)
Spike overlaps with street condition crisis (57 complaints THIS WEEK), suggesting possible causal relationship
reporting_angles: Are damaged streets and active construction projects driving traffic congestion? Map complaint locations to identify bottlenecks.
Interview DOT and traffic management about mitigation plans if construction is the driver.
